title: Tightening a Loose Door Handle
description: Turn a loose screw until the door handle sits firmly.
cardDescription: Turn a loose screw until the door handle sits firmly.
focus: The setting is tightening a Loose Door Handle. Match each clue to a thing, action, or description in that scene.
solvingTip: Begin with a short answer you recognize. Use its crossing letters to work toward the longer scene words.
words: Part held when carrying or using something
Movable panel at a room's entrance
Implement used to do a task
Material such as iron or copper
Rounded door handle turned by hand
Device secured or released with a door key
Small fastening holding a gate shut
Joint allowing a door to swing

answerNotes.HANDLE: A handle is the part made for the hand to grip. Its shape depends on whether the object is carried, pulled, poured, or turned.
answerNotes.SCREW: A screw has a spiral thread. Turning it moves it into material; a nail is usually driven with a hammer instead.
answerNotes.DOOR: A door is the movable panel at an entrance. Hinges let it swing, while a latch or lock holds it closed.
answerNotes.TOOL: A tool is an implement used to do a job. The clue may describe its action, such as cutting, turning, or gripping.
answerNotes.METAL: Metal names a family of materials including iron, copper, and aluminum. The word does not identify which metal a particular tool contains.
answerNotes.KNOB: A knob is a rounded control or handle. On an older television it may turn a setting; on a door it may operate a latch.
answerNotes.LOCK: A lock restricts access until the correct key or code is used. A latch holds a door closed without necessarily locking it.

words: Image made with a camera or pencil
Tool that checks a horizontal line
Upright side of a room or building
Pointed metal fastener struck by a hammer
Striking tool commonly used to drive nails
Writing tool with a graphite core
Put a sign or line on something
Sticky strip used to fasten paper
Find an object's size or length
Following a direct line without a curve

answerNotes.LEVEL: A level checks whether a surface is horizontal or vertical. It helps a frame hang straight without judging by sight alone.
answerNotes.FRAME: A frame surrounds and supports an image or object. The glass, backing, and outer border are separate parts of a picture frame.
answerNotes.HOOK: A fishing hook catches by its pointed curve. A wall hook is shaped for hanging objects rather than catching fish.
answerNotes.PENCIL: The writing core of a modern pencil is graphite, not metallic lead. Lead remains a traditional everyday name for it.
answerNotes.TAPE: Adhesive tape fastens surfaces with a sticky strip. Magnetic recording tape is a different material sharing the same short name.
answerNotes.HANG: Hang means support something from above. A hook, cord, or branch can hold the weight while the object hangs below.
answerNotes.GLASS: Glass is usually transparent but can also be colored. A glass is a drinking vessel, while glass without an article can name the material.

words: Underground part from which a tulip grows
Control that turns an electrical device on or off
Small fastener that grips papers together
Furniture with a flat top and legs
To follow and understand written words

answerNotes.LAMP: A lamp provides light from a fuel or electrical source. Bible lamps used oil rather than a modern bulb.
answerNotes.SHADE: Shade blocks direct sunlight. A shaded garden corner still receives some light; it is different from a completely dark room.
answerNotes.BULB: A bulb stores food for a plant underground. Tulips and daffodils grow from bulbs rather than from a packet of seed each spring.
answerNotes.LIGHT: Light makes things visible. A lamp produces light, while a mirror mainly reflects light arriving from elsewhere.
answerNotes.CORD: A cord can carry electricity or connect equipment. In an older telephone, the coiled cord let the handset move away from the base.
answerNotes.RIM: The rim is the edge around an opening. A flowerpot, glass, and bowl each have a rim, but not all rims are the same shape.
answerNotes.SCREW: A screw has a spiral thread. Turning it moves it into material; a nail is usually driven with a hammer instead.
answerNotes.TABLE: A table provides a raised flat surface. Chairs are the separate furniture used to sit beside it.

answerNotes.DOOR: A door is the movable panel at an entrance. Hinges let it swing, while a latch or lock holds it closed.
answerNotes.OIL: Oil has different uses in different scenes. It can be a cooking ingredient, lamp fuel, or part of a story about caring for a traveler.
answerNotes.SCREW: A screw has a spiral thread. Turning it moves it into material; a nail is usually driven with a hammer instead.
answerNotes.METAL: Metal names a family of materials including iron, copper, and aluminum. The word does not identify which metal a particular tool contains.
answerNotes.TOOL: A tool is an implement used to do a job. The clue may describe its action, such as cutting, turning, or gripping.
answerNotes.CLOTH: Cloth means fabric. A cloth used for wiping is an object made from that material, not a different substance.

words: Soft thick fabric made by pressing fibers together
Small soft cushion placed under something

answerNotes.CHAIR: A chair is intended for one sitter. A bench or sofa generally provides room for more than one person.
answerNotes.LEG: Leg can name a body part or a furniture support. Read the clue's setting before choosing between those ordinary meanings.
answerNotes.SOFT: Soft describes something that yields to touch. It can refer to cloth, an animal's fur, or food that is easy to bite.
answerNotes.CUT: Cut is an action, unlike a tool name such as scissors or knife. Matching the clue's part of speech helps narrow the answer.
answerNotes.SCISSORS: Scissors use two blades moving past one another. Finger loops help control the opening and closing action.
answerNotes.TABLE: A table provides a raised flat surface. Chairs are the separate furniture used to sit beside it.
answerNotes.WOOD: Wood comes from trees and has a grain. Following that grain when sanding usually leaves a smoother surface.
